![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14162956/assets/34e9beebbecc3eff77faa9b01f4684e334ec7cbdcbd9b00e328f95f7be88c1d4.png)

Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate the parabola shown above?
question.worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola is vertical, has its vertex at $(-2,4),$ and passes through the point $(2,2).$

The parametric equations of a vertical parabola that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ are

$$
x-h=2pt,\,y-k=p{t}^{2},
$$

where $p$ is constant.

In our case, $(h,k)=(-2,4),$ and so we have

$$
x+2=2pt,\,y-4=p{t}^{2}.
$$

Since the parabola passes through $(2,2),$ we can substitute $x=2$ and $y=2$ into the parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4=2pt \\ -2=p{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =2pt \\ 2 & =pt \\ t & =\frac{2}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the second equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2 & =p{(\frac{2}{p})}^{2} \\ -2 & =p\cdot \frac{4}{{p}^{2}} \\ -2 & =\frac{4}{p} \\ p & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x+2=2(-2)t,\,y-4=(-2){t}^{2},
$$

which simplify to

$$
x+2=-4t,\,y-4=-2{t}^{2}.
$$
